Meridian Regulation is resolved by the table, one question for both of its printed branches. Choose one of the target's poisons, diseases or physical impairments. If that effect makes the target repeat a saving throw, the target repeats that throw with Advantage, and a successful repeat applies the effect's own successful result. If the effect does not repeat its save, the target makes a Constitution saving throw with Advantage against that effect's printed DC (the number the throw has to beat), and on a success one of that effect's penalties -- Poisoned, a Speed reduction, Disadvantage on attack rolls, Disadvantage on ability checks, Disadvantage on saving throws, or an inability to take Reactions -- stops applying until the end of the target's next turn. Effects of either kind are all offered in the same question, so an effect that repeats its save never hides another effect from the printed choice. The fighter chooses which one.

The effect must be a poison, a disease, or a directly caused physical impairment before either branch is offered, and that is decided from the effect's own ability and its printed text, never from the penalty it happens to leave: a dream, an illusion or a sound that leaves one of the penalties below is still not one of those three. The fight keeps a reviewed list of the printed abilities that can leave such an effect, one entry for each ability with the sentence from the rules that decides it: an entry either places that ability in one of the three, or records that the ability stays the GM's to rule on. An ability that is on neither list is the GM's to rule on as well.

The two printed limits are checked before anything is offered: the effect must have a printed saving throw DC, and it must not carry the Curse, Tribulation, Foundation Injury, Hidden Injury, Possession, Permanent or Soul Damage tag. An effect with no printed DC, or one whose printed text the fight cannot identify, is the GM's to rule on. Disadvantage on attack rolls is also the GM's: the fight does not keep that penalty as a lasting mark of its own, so the GM applies it or waives it by hand.

Meridian Regulation does not automatically remove the underlying effect, end its duration, cure the disease or poison, remove Exhaustion, restore Hit Points, stop ongoing damage, or remove a higher-authority effect.
